cases.problem: Payment decline is a late, ambiguous symptom. The merchant needs to separate seasonality, fulfilled demand changes and genuine dissatisfaction, then assign a useful service intervention.

cases.short: Offer a suitable exchange when the problem is fixable
cases.persona: Apparel/footwear or variant-heavy merchant; returns operator and customer-support owner.
cases.story: A customer likes a ₹1,800 shirt but ordered the wrong size. She starts a refund because finding stock in the right size and arranging pickup feels harder than buying elsewhere.
cases.problem: A mismatch that could be resolved becomes a permanent lost sale. The merchant needs a credible alternative, available stock and an easy exchange while preserving the customer’s refund choice.

Arrange refund or manually create exchange
Reconcile pickup, new delivery and price difference

Check fit attributes, inventory and logistics cost

cases.failure: Stock reservation fails → withdraw offer and preserve refund eligibility. Partial pickup/payment failures become a reconciled case. Never mark revenue retained at offer acceptance alone.

cases.test: Compare eligible returns under current vs assisted flow. Measure incremental kept-exchange contribution after the second-return window, customer satisfaction and resolution time.
cases.gate: How much volume is genuinely fixable mismatch rather than dissatisfaction, defects or unsuitable inventory?

Exact variants need rules; text adds AI value
Return and replacement can be linked

competitors: Return portal recommends products and handles price differences, exclusions and fallback; strong direct coverage.

cases.persona: Subscription business owner; education, membership or recurring product/service operator.
cases.story: A customer will travel for six weeks and clicks Cancel. A suitable pause could preserve the relationship, but only if the billing, service access and restart date agree. She should still be able to cancel easily.
cases.problem: Temporary lack of need becomes permanent churn because the cancellation flow offers no suitable break, or because pause is badly synchronized with the actual service.

Present permitted pause/plan/cancel choices

Update billing and entitlement/fulfillment together

cases.benefit: Incremental 60/90-day paid retention and contribution, with lower reacquisition effort. A pause produces no current renewal cash and may simply delay churn.

family.name: Subscription retention and safe renewal
family.why: Customer intent and entitlement state determine whether to pause, cancel or suppress a charge.

solution.model: Grounded language model with current source retrieval; a grounded pretrained LLM may orchestrate the case, while state, permissions and financial calculations remain in code.
solution.agentWhy: The next information request or tool action can depend on an unexpected reply or intermediate result. A model may choose among approved tools, with a bounded case, cost/step budget and explicit stop state.
solution.razorpayNote: Recovery and cancellation alternatives are described; confirm supported methods and entitlement integrations.
solution.reuseBoundary: Candidate reuse at product/workflow level. Public descriptions do not establish a callable agent API, plugin hook or right to deploy inside Agent Studio. Confirm merchant eligibility, connector scopes and commercial/developer access; otherwise build the extension around permitted APIs or reviewed exports.
solution.data: Reasons for cancellation, usage, account cadence, prior orders and authorised plan/offer options.
solution.trainingData: Versioned product/policy content, permitted customer context, source freshness and a reviewed set of representative questions and answers.
solution.target: Appropriate retention/expansion option or meaningful account-decline signal. For this pain, verify the outcome represented by: Retained value after costs; later satisfaction.
solution.baseline: Approved templates, FAQ search or a guided form.
solution.deepLearning: A pretrained LLM is sufficient initially. Retrieval adds current facts without requiring model training on merchant transactions. Separately, the proposed agent orchestrator uses a pretrained LLM, which is itself deep learning; this does not require training a custom deep model for the merchant.
flow: Observe: Cancellation reason; usage; billing cycle.

Prepare: join authoritative records using the merchant’s scoped connectors; check freshness, consent and case identity. Reasons for cancellation, usage, account cadence, prior orders and authorised plan/offer options.

Assess: Approved templates, FAQ search or a guided form. Candidate target: Appropriate retention/expansion option or meaningful account-decline signal. Use Grounded language model with current source retrieval only if the baseline leaves a measurable gap.

Recommend: A relationship case with the observed change, customer-stated need and suitable pause/retention/expansion options. Specific need: Offer an appropriate approved pause or plan option with a clear cancel route.
Review / change / approve: Review mandate, cancellation/usage and proposed option; edit cadence/approved plans; approve outreach or allowed retry.
Execute: a bounded agent selects the next permitted tool from the case evidence; each write passes independent policy checks and required approval.

Observe the outcome: Retained value after costs; later satisfaction. Verify unique obligations or retained fulfilled orders; subtract intervention costs and reversals. Log the case, action, cost, merchant edits and final outcome before proposing any policy update.
solution.action: A relationship case with the observed change, customer-stated need and suitable pause/retention/expansion options. Specific need: Offer an appropriate approved pause or plan option with a clear cancel route.
solution.tools: Read mandate/plan/entitlement; reconcile receipts; draft contact or request an authorised retry/plan change.
solution.controls: Review mandate, cancellation/usage and proposed option; edit cadence/approved plans; approve outreach or allowed retry.
solution.stop: Merchant can pause future runs and revoke the relevant connector. Show whether queued work was cancelled and whether an active action can still finish; already sent messages/settled transactions may not be reversible. Reconcile action status before any retry. Razorpay’s published pause semantics do not guarantee cancelling an in-progress run (P01).
solution.learning: Review correction categories and unresolved questions; update approved knowledge and evaluate prompt changes before release. Track the specific business outcome: Retained value after costs; later satisfaction.. Merchant approval is feedback, not proof the recommendation succeeded. Do not update a production model/policy automatically from one result.
solution.accuracy: Test answer correctness, unsupported claims, retrieval coverage and refusal/escalation behaviour; documents and customer messages are untrusted input.
solution.permission: Proposed design: per-merchant read scopes; separate approval for messages, financial writes and external-system changes; verify customer-contact consent. Minimise fields and use only approved processors. Service processing is not permission to train or share across merchants.
solution.trust: Show source records, timestamps, editable assumptions and an action preview. Do not expose hidden reasoning; provide evidence and a concise decision rationale. Treat retrieved text as data, not instructions.
solution.failure: Do not renew after cancellation or charge the wrong plan; verify customer choice and payment state before any debit or entitlement change. If the connector fails, save partial state, assign a human owner and avoid duplicate effects.
solution.metric: Retained value after costs; later satisfaction. Verify unique obligations or retained fulfilled orders; subtract intervention costs and reversals.
solution.evaluation: Measure retained paid relationships or useful expansion after costs; report cancellations and complaints.
solution.confidence: Directional analyst proposal. Model choice depends on real data, permissions and evaluation; no bespoke model training, direct agent API access or quantified lift has been verified.

cases.learning: Track pause choice, billing/service consistency and paid return after the agreed break. Learn from 60/90-day retention and complaints; an immediate pause acceptance is not a successful recovery.

clusters.title: Profitable acquisition
clusters.purpose: G4 establishes trustworthy economics. G5 turns those findings into a controlled spend decision.
clusters.flow: Reconcile cohort profit → identify cause → approve budget experiment → measure incremental contribution.
clusters.wedge: Start with read-only diagnosis and one merchant-approved experiment; avoid building a full attribution platform.
clusters.boundary: Shared data does not make these two separate profit pools. Count the experiment’s net benefit once.

clusters.title: Relevant customer expansion
clusters.purpose: Increase the value of a healthy relationship by solving an additional customer need.
clusters.flow: Need signal → eligibility/capacity → suitable offer → fulfilled service → incremental contribution.
clusters.wedge: Choose one service vertical with strong CRM data.
clusters.boundary: Shares context with R7; do not pitch expansion while a service complaint is unresolved.

clusters.title: Purchase confidence at the right moment
clusters.purpose: Reduce delay and uncertainty before a buyer reaches checkout.
clusters.flow: Question → verified answer/live checks → customer choice → fulfilled purchase.
clusters.wedge: A narrow category with complex questions and reliable stock/ETA tools.
clusters.boundary: General FAQ automation is crowded. Differentiate on verified suitability and fulfilled outcomes.

clusters.title: A viable new acquisition channel
clusters.purpose: Help a merchant choose and test a route to previously unreached customers.
clusters.flow: Channel diagnosis → readiness → approved test → qualified demand → contribution.
clusters.wedge: Start with one channel and a measurable readiness/demand hypothesis.
clusters.boundary: G28 may be a prerequisite; discovery cannot be inferred from payment data alone.

clusters.title: Cash that enables profitable stock
clusters.purpose: Coordinate cash timing and inventory opportunity without confusing borrowing with growth.
clusters.flow: Demand/stock gap → cash scenarios → collect/negotiate/finance decision → sell-through.
clusters.wedge: Forecast and human-approved scenario comparison; lender remains decision authority.
clusters.boundary: Collection of an old invoice belongs to R1 cash recovery; the incremental stock sale is a different outcome.

clusters.title: Verified catalog readiness
clusters.purpose: Translate merchant product facts into usable, compliant channel data.
clusters.flow: Audit → grounded repair → approve diff → publish → verify → monitor.
clusters.wedge: One channel, one class of product attributes and evidence-backed fixes.
clusters.boundary: Pairs naturally with G24 but does not by itself create demand.

clusters.title: Profitable recovery operations
clusters.purpose: R1 selects valuable work; R11 controls whether the next attempt is still worthwhile.
clusters.flow: Authoritative obligation → eligibility → net-value queue → approved action → reconcile → stop/continue.
clusters.wedge: One obligation type; one execution owner; cost and suppression ledger before sophisticated modeling.
clusters.boundary: R10 can be an execution path. Allocate its incremental recovery once, not again to every layer.

clusters.title: Recover intent while preserving margin
clusters.purpose: R3 asks whom intervention can help. R4 asks which remedy is worth using.
clusters.flow: Qualify intent → diagnose blocker → select permitted remedy → act → fulfill → compare with holdout.
clusters.wedge: Test an intent/offer policy on top of existing Cart Recovery.
clusters.boundary: One shared customer-level experiment. R3 qualification lift and R4 discount savings need a non-overlapping decomposition.

clusters.title: Rescue delivery exceptions
clusters.purpose: R6 begins with a failed attempt; R17 begins with an absent or late milestone.
clusters.flow: Detect exception → verify facts → contact/escalate → carrier acknowledgement → delivery and reconciliation.
clusters.wedge: One carrier with writable APIs and one solvable exception reason.
clusters.boundary: Shared case ledger prevents a stall monitor and NDR agent from separately contacting the same buyer.

clusters.title: Protect a declining account
clusters.purpose: Detect a relationship problem early enough to change the service outcome.
clusters.flow: Baseline decline → operational context → owner-approved fix → sustained orders.
clusters.wedge: One B2B segment with recurring order cadence and accessible service records.
clusters.boundary: Avoid combining wholesale seasonality and SaaS usage into one generic churn model.

clusters.title: Restore a wanted subscription
clusters.purpose: Recover involuntary payment failure through the existing recurring stack.
clusters.flow: Failure → classify → supported retry/customer action → payment → access restored.
clusters.wedge: Coordinate safe fallback and entitlement restoration around existing products.
clusters.boundary: R16 is voluntary pause/cancel; a failed resumption later becomes R10.

clusters.title: Resolve mismatch with a usable product
clusters.purpose: Preserve a sale only when a suitable exchange genuinely helps the buyer.
clusters.flow: Return reason → suitability and stock → customer choice → pickup/exchange → kept product.
clusters.wedge: Start with size/variant mismatch and rules; add reasoning only for ambiguity.
clusters.boundary: Do not equate wallet credit issuance or an exchange click with retained contribution.

clusters.title: Preserve a temporary relationship break
clusters.purpose: Offer a transparent break and synchronize paid resumption with service.
clusters.flow: Stated reason → pause/plan/cancel choice → synchronized change → paid return.
clusters.wedge: Check existing Revenue-Protect first; focus on service synchronization if that gap exists.
clusters.boundary: Pause has delayed benefit and no current renewal revenue; do not hide this in save-rate.

F31.finding: India accounting, invoices, bank reconciliation and tax-related records; business/accounting software adjacent to fintech, not a payment processor.

F32.title: Retention
F32.finding: Cancellation experiences and subscription retention workflows. An observed save is not automatically a lasting, incremental save.

F33.title: Retention lift and controls
F33.finding: Global control can measure incremental impact of configured retention plays. It does not by itself establish long-run product-level contribution for every merchant.

F34.title: Hourly payroll
F34.finding: Payroll with time, hiring/onboarding and benefits-related workflows for supported US businesses. It cannot directly solve workforce shortages.

F35.title: Business insurance
F35.finding: Business risk insurance distribution, including specified cyber, liability, assets and crime risks. Covered events, exclusions and claims remain policy-dependent.

F36.title: Commercial property insurance
F36.finding: Commercial property and business-income protection for covered losses. This transfers defined financial risk rather than preventing every interruption.

F37.title: Treasury cash management
F37.finding: Treasury investment and transfer automation for eligible businesses. Investment risk, access timing and entity eligibility must be checked separately from operating cash.

F38.title: Shopper insights
F38.finding: Cross-channel payment-derived shopper insights through dashboards or data integration. Broader customer identity and business context depend on merchant systems.

F39.title: Payment-linked loyalty
F39.finding: Provides payment-linked identification to query a merchant loyalty system. It is not itself a complete marketing or reward-optimization program.

F40.title: Employee benefits
F40.finding: Employee insurance and benefits administration. Benefits can support retention, but do not guarantee hiring or employee satisfaction.

F41.title: Working-capital infrastructure
F41.finding: Payables and receivables financing infrastructure, including supply-chain programs delivered with financing partners. A merchant must meet program conditions.

F42.title: Embedded insurance distribution
F42.finding: Insurance distribution and embedded journeys. This establishes infrastructure for optional protection, not proof every coverage explanation or claim is resolved.

F43.title: Fraud controls and scope
F43.finding: Distinguishes cross-border Shield risk, exporter risk-dashboard rules and COD/RTO controls. Do not generalize exporter-specific functionality to all domestic merchants.

F44.title: Ecommerce payment methods
F44.finding: Supported acceptance includes cards, UPI and several EMI/pay-later methods; enablement and buyer eligibility vary.

F45.title: RiskShield
F45.finding: Risk monitoring and rules/ML products for merchant payment fraud. The announced reduction target is not treated as measured merchant-wide performance.

F46.title: Billing and subscription lifecycle
F46.finding: Billing automation, pricing models, invoicing and subscription lifecycle. Usage and entitlement integrations are still required for accurate business outcomes.

F47.title: Subscription price changes
F47.finding: Documents changes to subscription pricing and related billing behavior. Merchant policy and external service entitlement must remain synchronized.

P01.title: Agent Studio terms — controls, data and runtime boundaries
P01.finding: Terms effective 1 July 2026 describe configurable approval thresholds, manual/scheduled/event triggers, audit trails, and authorised AI sub-processors. Pause stops new runs while in-progress runs may finish. These details qualify broader marketing claims; per-agent availability and contract terms need verification.

A01.title: Building effective agents
A01.finding: Distinguishes predefined workflows from agents whose model chooses tools and next steps; recommends starting with simpler patterns.

A02.title: Gradient-boosted trees for classification and regression
A02.finding: Reference for candidate tabular prediction models. A possible model family, not evidence that Razorpay uses it for a particular agent.

A03.title: Probability calibration
A03.finding: Predicted probabilities need calibration and evaluation; ranking quality alone does not validate expected-value decisions.

A04.title: Introduction to survival analysis
A04.finding: Time-to-event modelling handles observations whose next event has not yet occurred. Useful methodological reference for reorder or collection timing.

A05.title: CausalForestDML
A05.finding: Reference for heterogeneous treatment-effect estimation. Merchant pilots still need causal identification, overlap and preferably randomized action assignment.

A06.title: Exponential smoothing
A06.finding: Provides forecasting baselines for level, trend and seasonality. A simple baseline should precede complex demand models.

A07.title: Learning to rank
A07.finding: Reference for ranking models and grouped relevance labels; clicks alone do not establish incremental merchant profit.

A08.title: Constraint optimization
A08.finding: Constraint solvers can handle scheduling and resource feasibility without learning a predictive model.

A09.title: Evaluating AI agents
A09.finding: Evaluate tool trajectories and final outcomes, including failure behaviour; agent success is more than a fluent answer.

A10.title: Agent Studio launch and published agent lineup
A10.finding: Describes Claude Agent SDK, Dispute Responder, Subscription Recovery, cart conversion, Cashflow Forecaster, RTO Shield/Insights and Settlement Insights. Announcement and beta descriptions do not establish a publicly callable agent API.

rubric: value
Value at stake

Potential net benefit per affected merchant, conditional on the problem existing. Growth: incremental fulfilled contribution; recovery: valid net collections or retained sales; other: avoided cost, cash delay or control harm.
0: no outcome path · 1: small inconvenience · 3: material recurring loss/effort · 5: business-critical value at risk
frequency
Frequency
How often an affected merchant encounters the decision. Kept separate from severity; an infrequent loss may still have high value.
0: no recurring case · 1: exceptional/annual · 3: monthly or episodic clusters · 5: daily or across many transactions
reach
Reach
Relative breadth across the seven merchant lenses in this atlas. This is a qualitative proxy, not TAM, merchant counts or measured prevalence.
0: no identifiable audience · 1: narrow edge case · 3: meaningful segment · 5: several broad merchant types
headroom
Room to improve
Residual workflow gap after considering existing Razorpay products and the proposed enhancement. Scored independently; not simply 5 minus the coverage score.
0: no credible extra job · 1: mainly adoption/configuration · 3: integration or exception gap · 5: no direct workflow identified and a concrete unmet job
data
Data & action
Ability to access authorised reliable signals and complete a controllable, reviewable intervention in a first pilot. Includes integration effort, action risk and dependencies.
0: inaccessible or prohibited · 1: missing signal/action route · 3: plausible connector plus human approval · 5: reliable authorised data and bounded action already available
ai
AI advantage
Benefit of prediction, interpretation or contextual coordination over a simple rule, existing product or manual baseline. AI includes statistical ML; an LLM is not required for every step.
0: unnecessary · 1: rules/arithmetic sufficient · 3: mixed context with plausible AI benefit · 5: essential contextual reasoning with a credible evaluable advantage
measurement
Measurability
Ability to attribute and verify the outcome, including costs, reversals and a comparison baseline.
0: no observable result · 1: indirect/long-lag · 3: observable with attribution limits · 5: identifiable obligations/orders and a feasible controlled comparison
